tasks.title: Per-target C++17 and AUTOMOC/AUTOUIC
tasks.note:
REJECTED
- Examples/CMakeLists.txt: the tests TargetProperties_HandPaintingExample and TargetProperties_HandPaintingExampleTests still pass when their own `target_compile_features(... PRIVATE cxx_std_17)` lines are removed (checked, then restored). `$<TARGET_PROPERTY:tgt,COMPILE_FEATURES>` is transitive, so it picks up the PUBLIC cxx_std_17 from HandPaintingExampleLib; the test does not prove the executable and test targets set it themselves. Fix: read a non-transitive property for the per-target check (e.g. parse the target's own flags, or check that the `target_compile_features` line is present for each target), or make the lib's feature PRIVATE/INTERFACE so only a target's own setting can satisfy its test. In every case confirm the test fails when the line is removed.
Everything else is fine (fresh build and ctest 10/10; no globals in project CMake files; scan excludes specs/.worktrees/build dirs with an empty-scan guard; AUTOMOC on lib/app/tests, AUTOUIC on lib).
tasks.review:
APPROVED
- ProjectFiles (Examples/tests/ProjectFiles.cmake): scans all CMakeLists.txt and *.cmake files and fails on CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD, CMAKE_AUTOMOC or CMAKE_AUTOUIC; fails if the root CMakeLists.txt was not scanned, so it cannot pass on an empty scan.
- TargetProperties_HandPaintingExampleLib, _HandPaintingExample, _HandPaintingExampleTests and _hpq check each target's own cxx_std_17, and AUTOMOC ON for the three Qt targets; the lib also needs AUTOUIC ON. Removing each target's own target_compile_features line in turn made exactly that target's test fail (files restored). Removing AUTOMOC or AUTOUIC from the lib made its test fail. AUTOMOC removal on the executable and the tests target was not tried.
- Fresh configure, build and ctest: 10/10 passed.
